cp-excitation-energy-definition: Section 1, p.2: the CP approach is defined in two numbered steps and Eq. (3); read in context.
lr-excitation-energy-definition: Section 1, p.3: LR energies are defined as the resonant energies of the linearized dynamics, Eqs. (4)-(5); the symplectic-eigenvalue form is stated under a nondegeneracy assumption, as the value says.
cp-spurious-critical-points: Section 1, p.2: the authors state that CP has spurious critical points and Morse-index mismatch, and show it in Fig. 1 and Section 5.2. Morse-index mismatch cites ref. 52.
kahler-unifies-cp-lr: Section 1, p.2: the paper states the formalism also applies to adiabatic TDDFT, with the stated reason (intrinsic Kaehler structure, cites 43,44) and the stated caveat.
kahler-dynamics-definition: Section 1, p.2, Eqs. (1)-(2): the dynamics and its steady states are defined.
energy-conserved-hamiltonian-dynamics: Section 2, p.5: orthogonality of the velocity to the gradient follows from Eq. (7), g(u,Ju)=0, shown in the text; energy conservation follows directly. Derivation is complete in the paper, though not a labeled theorem.
ghf-scope-assumptions: Section 3.4, p.13: the paper states it focuses on GHF and assumes no external magnetic field and no spin-orbit coupling. The 'easily adapted' remark is an authors' claim, not a result.
fci-both-exact: cross-group consistency, Rule A (coordinator, 2026-10-30): Sec. 3.3, pp.12-13: the paper derives both halves: CP critical points are the excited states, giving omega_k = E_k - E_0, and the LR equation (35) on the tangent space reduces to dPsi/dt = -i(H restricted - E_0)Psi, giving the same energies. 'We recover the well-known fact' says the result is not new; it is still proved in the paper with linear algebra only. Being well known is not a cited step. The reviewer's suggestion was high, proved result.
non-physical-eta-caveat: Section 4, p.15: the authors state that eta different from 1 is non-physical, a caveat on their own analysis.
assumption-H-nondegenerate: Section 4, p.16: Assumption (H) is the paper's stated assumption; the degeneracy consequence follows in one line.
lemma1-symplectic-perturbation: Lemma 1, Appendix A.3, p.31-32: stated with its conditions (block-diagonal A(eta), distinct positive omega_i^0, distinct lambda_i,+-) and proved immediately after, using first-order perturbation theory.
numerics-setup-uhf: Section 5.1, p.19: bases, systems, eta range and the CP tracking rule are stated as the paper's setup.
numerics-setup-geometry: Section 5.1, p.19: the geometries are stated as the paper's setup.
numerics-tools: Section 5, p.18-19: the methods and PySCF use are stated as the paper's computational setup.
h4-saddle-search-setup: Section 5.2, p.21: the system, eta grid and 50 random starts are stated as setup.
h4-fci-projection-setup: Section 5.2, p.21: the 36-state count and the choice of the eight lowest states are stated as the paper's setup.
limitation-preliminary-numerics: Section 6, p.24: the authors call the simulations preliminary, state the index-1 restriction, and urge caution on physical meaning.
future-work-casscf: Section 6, p.24: CASSCF formalization is deferred to Part II, so this paper does not cover it. The 'post-HF is more accurate' remark is a general claim, not what grades this.
projector-definition: Sec. II B, p.4: the paper defines a projector and the indicator analogy in context.
conjunction-requires-commutation: Sec. II B, p.4: the paper sets conjunction of projectors as PQ when P and Q commute; the statement is correct and is how CH defines conjunction.
ch-conjunction-meaningless-noncommuting: Sec. II B, p.4: the paper states that CH treats noncommuting conjunction as meaningless and limits reasoning to frameworks.
pdi-definition: Sec. II B, p.4: the PDI and its event algebra are defined.
single-framework-rule: Sec. II B, p.4: the single framework rule is stated as a principle of CH.
history-pdi-definition: Sec. II B, p.5: the history PDI is defined.
single-framework-rule-extended: Sec. II B, p.5: the extended rule is stated as part of CH for closed systems with the extended Born rule.
mz-setup-photon-exits-c: Sec. III A, p.7: the gedanken setup is stated ('let us suppose') as the paper's scenario.
spin-two-families-px-pz: Sec. III B, p.9: the two PDIs Px and Pz are the paper's stated example setup.
spin-details-omitted: Sec. III B, p.9: the author states that details of the apparatus description are omitted from the spin discussion.
quasiclassical-exceptions-chaos: Sec. IV, p.10: the author states that the quasiclassical argument is plausible only if exceptions such as classical chaos are excluded; the chaos remark itself is a field statement.
quasiclassical-needs-further-study: Sec. IV, p.10: the author admits the cited ideas need further study.

theory_low.flat-space-classical-hamiltonian: Section 2, p.6: the equivalence with Eq. (10) is asserted with H_cl(q,p)=E(q+ip) but not computed. The value adds the interpretive 'generalizes' claim, which the paper words as 'can be interpreted'.
theory_low.fig1-toy-model-spurious: Figure 1, p.3: an illustration of the authors' claim on a toy function whose formula is not in the text; the point b' is called spurious by the authors, not proved.
theory_low.fci-cp-lr-coincide: Section 3.3, p.12-13: the paper calls this the well-known FCI fact, not a labeled theorem. The value drops the stated condition that the ground state is nondegenerate (simple E0) for the symplectic-eigenvalue claim, and the CP half is stated without proof.
theory_low.tdhf-mcweeny-correspondence: Section 3.4, p.14: the authors identify Eq. (29) with TDHF and (30) with the McWeeny form in one sentence, with no derivation. An identification with known equations.
theory_low.ghf-casida-alternative: Section 3.4, p.14: 'simple alternative to Casida' is the authors' claim; the A and B matrices are a derived result agreeing with Ref. 69, not a theorem.
theory_low.ghf-A-B-definition: Section 3.4, p.14: A and B are deduced from Eq. (32), not defined from nothing, and the agreement with Ref. 69 is a cited cross-check. A derived expression, not a labeled proved result.
theory_low.fci-weak-coupling-analytic: Section 4.1, p.16: rests on 'standard nondegenerate perturbation theory', a cited standard result, not proved in the paper.
theory_low.fci-first-order-triplet-lowest: Section 4.1, p.17, Eq. (41): a first-order perturbation result derived in Appendix A.1, not a labeled theorem. Eq. (41) and the A.1 print differ in the sign of some terms, so the printed formula is not settled.
theory_low.cp-uhf-isolated-critical-points: Section 4.2, p.17: stated under (H) by an appeal to the analytic implicit function theorem; no proof is given. An authors' derivation, not a labeled theorem.
theory_low.cp-uhf-homo-lumo-first-order: Section 4.2 and Appendix A.2: a derived first-order perturbation expression, not a labeled theorem or proposition.
theory_low.lr-uhf-number-of-excitations: Section 4.2, p.18: a dimension count and an interpretation at eta=0, stated in two sentences without proof.
theory_low.lr-uhf-matches-fci-first-order: Section 4.2, p.18, Eq. (47): a result from the A.3 derivation (it uses proved Lemma 1) but not itself a labeled theorem; the authors' claim of coincidence.
theory_low.cp-differs-from-fci-first-order: Section 6, p.24: a conclusion sentence summarizing the authors' results, including their word 'correct'. Not a proved statement.
theory_low.la-uhf-recovers-eq47: Appendix A.3, p.33: a remark that a derivation recovers Eq. (47). A computation step, not a labeled result.
theory_low.la-uhf-not-identical-note: Appendix A.3, p.33: a one-line remark comparing derivatives; not a defined, proved or limiting statement.
theory_low.appendix-a1-sign-print: Appendix A.1, p.29 against Eq. (41), p.17: a print inconsistency between two formulas (other cross-spin terms also differ in sign), not an authored claim. Does not settle any value.
theory_low.conclusion-single-excitations-orbital-re: Section 6, p.24: the authors' conclusion, with TDHF/TDDFT limits a field statement; not proved here.
theory_low.conclusion-cp-lr-coincide-fci-differ-non: Section 6, p.24: a conclusion summary of the authors' analytic results; the weakly interacting equivalence is argued, not stated as a theorem.
theory_low.bs-fraction-detection: Sec. III A, p.7: the Born-rule frequency expectation, a field statement not shown in the paper.
theory_low.spin-no-projector-for-conjunction: Sec. III B, p.8: a Hilbert-space fact stated flatly, without a proof.
theory_low.spin-px-probability-one: Sec. III B, p.9: the conditional probability is stated without the computation; a result asserted, not shown.
theory_low.spin-pz-intermediate-value: Sec. III B, p.9: a conclusion stated without the computation.
theory_low.spin-no-simultaneous-combination: Sec. III B, p.9: an application of the single framework rule, stated as interpretation.
theory_low.harrison-laplacian-k-dependent-scatterin: Section 3, p.6: 'typically dependent' is an informal remark after Eq. (3.1); no condition or proof is stated.
theory_low.harrison-standard-vertex-k-independent: Section 3, p.6: an example given by the matrices in (3.2) and the formula (3.3), with no proof or conditions beyond the example.
theory_low.harrison-most-unitary-not-laplacian: Section 3, p.6: 'most' is argued informally from Prop. 3.1; no count or measure is given.
theory_low.harrison-dirac-scattering-matrix-k-indep: Section 4, p.9: unitarity is cited to ref. [4]; k-independence follows from gamma=1 stated without proof.
theory_low.harrison-any-kindependent-matrix-realize: Section 4, p.9, Eq. (4.11): a construction asserted with one line, no proof written out.
theory_low.harrison-no-spin-rotation-factorization: Section 4, p.9: the factorization is described in prose, with no formal proof.
theory_low.harrison-multiplicity-two-kramers: Section 4, p.9: stated without proof; the Kramers statement is deferred to ref. [4].
theory_low.harrison-main-result: Section 4, p.9 and Abstract: the authors' own 'we observe' with prose argument; no theorem with conditions and proof.
theory_low.adiabatic-elimination-pair-probabilities: Eq. (3), p.2: an approximate solution stated without derivation; the text layer lost the comparison signs.
theory_low.isolated-rabi-subspace: Discussion of Fig. 1, p.3: a qualitative statement about the model, with no proof.
theory_low.high-fidelity-pair-at-pi-over-2: After Eq. (3), p.3: an approximate consequence of Eq. (3), not separately proved; the paper's 'high fidelity' is the authors' claim.
